sections.h2: Who sets and who collects property tax in Laurel County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work in Laurel County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assesses the property, the Laurel County Sheriff collects the bill, and the Laurel County Clerk takes over any bill left unpaid after the collection season ends. Knowing which desk handles which step saves a seller a lot of phone calls.

  • PVA: Room 127, 101 S. Main St., London, KY 40741. Open Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 4:30. Phone (606) 864-2889. The office's website searches parcels by address, owner or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Phone 606-864-6600. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:00, and the office is closed Saturday and Sunday.
  • Clerk: Room 203, 101 S. Main St., London. Phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk runs the delinquent tax sale.

The PVA decides what the house is worth for tax purposes. Ask the sheriff or the PVA for the rate that applies to a specific parcel, since a countywide average will not match every address.

sections.h2: What is Laurel County like as a place to own a house?
sections.html:
Laurel County was established on December 21, 1825 and covers roughly 434 square miles of land. London is the county seat and largest city. Corbin sits mostly in Whitley County but reaches into Laurel and Knox. Part of the Daniel Boone National Forest and Laurel River Lake fall inside the county line, and the Battle of Wildcat Mountain in the Civil War was fought here. The original Kentucky Fried Chicken cafe near Corbin and the World Chicken Festival in London are the county's best-known draws.

  • Population: 63,746 estimated for July 2025, with a 2020 density of 144 people per square mile.
  • Housing: 27,063 units, 23,996 households and an owner occupancy rate of 71.6 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $159,500. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,239, while owners with none report $382.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 21, according to the Census Bureau.

sections.h2: When does a Laurel County property tax bill have to be paid?
sections.html:
Assessment day is January 1, and the bill is payable to the sheriff by December 31 of that assessment year. KRS 134.015 attaches a price tag to timing, and the schedule is the same in every Kentucky county that bills on the regular calendar.

  • Paid in full on or before November 1: 2 percent off.
  • Paid from November 2 through December 31: the printed amount.
  • Paid during January: 5 percent added.
  • Paid after January 31: 10 percent added.

If the usual schedule is delayed, the state may set an alternative one, with the tax due two full months after the bills are mailed and the discount lasting one month. The sheriff accepts payment in person, by mail or at the drop box on the front of the building. Mailed or dropped payments should be checks, never cash, and a receipt needs a stamped self-addressed envelope. Cards are taken inside the office.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Laurel County assessment?
sections.html:
An owner who disagrees with the PVA's value must first sit down with the PVA or a deputy for a conference. Only after that conference can an appeal go to the local board of assessment appeals. The state's calendar lays out the steps.

  • The real property tax roll is open for public inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May, Saturdays included.
  • An appeal is filed at the county clerk's office by the end of the next workday after the inspection period closes.
  • The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends, usually for no more than five days.
  • The owner brings evidence such as sales listings, insurance papers, construction cost and a description of the land and buildings. Without it the board denies the appeal.

An owner who skips the board hearing cannot go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If tax bills go out before the appeal finishes, the bill is based on the value the owner claimed, and a supplemental bill follows if the board sets a higher figure.

sections.h2: Does Laurel County offer relief for older or disabled owners?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption lowers the assessed value of the home for owners who are 65 or older or who are classified as totally disabled. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years it removes $49,100 from the assessment, so a house assessed at $200,000 is taxed on $150,900. The application goes to the Laurel County PVA at the Room 127 office.

Age is proven with a birth certificate, driver's license, passport or similar record. A disability claim needs classification as totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program, with payments received through the whole assessment period. Disability owners reapply every year unless they are veterans with a service connected disability, or have been found totally and permanently disabled by the Social Security Administration or the Kentucky Retirement Systems. A seller who qualifies should ask the PVA how the exemption is handled once the house sells.

sections.h2: What happens to a Laurel County tax bill that goes unpaid?
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the county clerk, where it becomes a certificate of delinquency and a lien is recorded against the property. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, and the clerk and county attorney add commissions. The state's worked example starts with a $1,000 bill, which grows to $1,254 when it moves, using an assumed sheriff commission of 4 percent.

What a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill costs at each stage of delinquency (Department of Revenue worked examples)
StageTotal due
Moved from sheriff to clerk$1,254.00
Paid within five business days of the transfer$1,387.79
Paid after the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
Paid in May, with a second month of interest$1,627.61
Paid after the June advertisement$1,659.90
Bought by a third party at the clerk's sale$1,704.21

A tax sale is set at least 90 days, and no more than 135 days, after the transfer to the clerk. The lien stays on the land for up to eleven years under KRS 134.015, no matter who owns it. The clerk's 2026 sale notice put registration for third party buyers between August 17 and 31, and that period is over.

sections.h2: What should a Laurel County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
• Ask the sheriff for the current bill and any older unpaid year before you list.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate of delinquency exists against the parcel.
  • Look up the parcel on the PVA website to confirm the owner name and the assessed value.
  • If you are 65 or older or disabled, check whether the homestead exemption is on file, and expect it to be reviewed after the sale.
  • Agree with the buyer in the contract how the year's bill will be split at closing.

A seller who would rather sell as is can ask for a direct offer. Any tax owed still gets paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Laurel County?
faqs.a: At the Laurel County Sheriff's Office, 1380 East Hwy 192 in London. The office takes payment in person, by mail and at its drop box, and accepts cards at the counter.

faqs.q: What discount does Laurel County give for paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent, if the bill is paid in full by November 1 of the assessment year. KRS 134.015 sets that discount for the regular schedule.

faqs.q: Who do I call to question a Laurel County assessment?
faqs.a: The Laurel County PVA at (606) 864-2889. A conference with the PVA or a deputy comes before any appeal to the board.

faqs.q: How much is the Kentucky homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It applies to owners 65 or older and to owners classified as totally disabled, and it is claimed at the PVA's office.

faqs.q: Can unpaid property tax follow a house to a new owner?
faqs.a: Yes. Under KRS 134.015 the lien from delinquent taxes continues for the eleven year period regardless of who owns the property, so buyers and title agents look for it before closing.
